mesa_runner package¶

Public package exports for mesa-runner.

This module re-exports the primary user-facing classes and functions from submodules so common workflows can be accessed from a single import point.

set_options(defaults, *, options=None, controls=None, star_job=None, binary_controls=None, binary_job=None, kap=None, eos=None, pgstar=None, pgbinary=None)[source]¶
Method that allows for MESA options to be set in bulk and optionally

ordered based on the MESA namelist they belong to.

Parameters:

  • defaults (DefaultsOptions) – DefaultsOptions object that holds all information about MESA defaults

  • options (dict[str, object] | None) – Dictionary with all specified options to be added to the Inlist object. Allows options from all namelists to be mixed, but will throw an error if one or more of the options is part of more than one MESA namelist. In that case, the namelist-specific dictionaries should be used.

  • kap (dict[str, object] | None)

None

set_mesa_env(*, mesasdk_root, omp_num_threads=None, apply_to_process=True, shell_executable='/bin/bash', base_env=None)[source]¶

Set the MESA_DIR and MESASDK_ROOT variables and execute the initialisation scripts.

Parameters:

  • mesasdk_root (Path | str) – Location of the MESA SDK directory (MESASDK_ROOT)

  • omp_num_threads (int | None) – Number of CPU threads to use for a single MESA run (OMP_NUM_THREADS).

  • apply_to_process (bool)

  • shell_executable (Path | str)

  • base_env (Mapping[str, str] | None)

Return type:

dict[str, str]

apply_to_process: If True, update the current Python process environment (os.environ)

with the resolved MESA/MESASDK variables, so later code in this process automatically sees them. If False, do not modify os.environ; the method still returns the environment dictionary, which you can pass explicitly to subprocess calls.

shell_executable: Path to the shell used to run the MESASDK init script.

Most users should keep the default “/bin/bash”. Change this only if your system requires a different shell executable.

base_env:

Optional starting environment mapping. If None, the current process environment (os.environ) is used. Provide this when you want a controlled or reproducible environment (for example in tests, CI, or isolated runs). Values from MESA setup always override base_env for MESA_DIR, MESASDK_ROOT, and OMP_NUM_THREADS.

Returns:

The returned dict is the final runtime environment after sourcing MESASDK and applying explicit MESA variables. If apply_to_process is True, this final environment is also written to os.environ.

Return type:

env

Parameters:

  • mesasdk_root (Path | str)

  • omp_num_threads (int | None)

  • apply_to_process (bool)

  • shell_executable (Path | str)

  • base_env (Mapping[str, str] | None)

mesa_runner.launch_model_process(model, *, env=None, sync_before_run=True, default_options=None, config=None, allow_unknown_options=False, command_name='rn', log_file_name='log.out', observer=None, live_registry=None)[source]¶
Function to launch a single model in a non-blocking way.

The function performs preflight checks, starts the MESA model run and immediately returns with the RunHandle and process ID for tracking. Use this if you want to run a MESA model “in the background”.

Parameters:

  • model (Model) – Model to launch.

  • env (Mapping[str, str] | None) – Optional runtime environment to launch the MESA model into.

  • sync_before_run (bool) – If True (default), the function calls work_setup.sync_model_with_disk to update the inlist attributes of Model in case the user made any changes to the inlist files themselves. This ensures that the inlist files themselves remain the ground truth.

  • default_options (DefaultsOptions | None) – DefaultOptions object. Should be passed if sync_before_run == True.

  • config (MesaConfig | None) – MesaConfig object. Will be reconstructed on the fly if not passed.

  • allow_unknown_options (bool) – If True, give a warning about inlist options that are not found in the defaults files when syncing Model.inlists with inlists in the model directory. If False, raise an exception when inlist options are found that are not found in the defaults files.

  • command_name (str) – Name of the “rn” script. Can be changed to custom “rn” script names.

  • log_file_name (str) – Name of the terminal log file that will be placed inside the model directory. Default is “log.out”

  • observer (RunObserver | None) – RunObserver object that observes StateTransitions for status and repository admin.

  • live_registry (LiveProcessRegistry | None)

Returns:

Tuple containing RunHandle and subprocess ID.

Raises:

  • ValueError – If sync_before_run is True and no DefaultsOptions object is passed

  • RunLaunchError – If model failed to launch

Return type:

tuple[RunHandle, Popen]

mesa_runner.run_model(model, *, env=None, sync_before_run=True, default_options=None, config=None, allow_unknown_options=False, command_name='rn', log_file_name='log.out', capture_output=True, timeout=None, observer=None, live_registry=None)[source]¶
Function to launch a single model in a blocking way.

The function calls launch_model_process and wait_for_model_process immediately afterwards. It will only return once the model has finished running. Use this to run a MESA model “on the foreground” as you would do with a regular MESA “./rn” call in the terminal.

Parameters:

  • model (Model) – Model to run.

  • env (Mapping[str, str] | None) – Optional runtime environment to launch the MESA model into.

  • sync_before_run (bool) – If True (default), the function calls work_setup.sync_model_with_disk to update the inlist attributes of Model in case the user made any changes to the inlist files themselves. This ensures that the inlist files themselves remain the ground truth.

  • default_options (DefaultsOptions | None) – DefaultOptions object. Should be passed if sync_before_run == True.

  • config (MesaConfig | None) – MesaConfig object. Will be reconstructed on the fly if not passed.

  • allow_unknown_options (bool) – If True, give a warning about inlist options that are not found in the defaults files when syncing Model.inlists with inlists in the model directory. If False, raise an exception when inlist options are found that are not found in the defaults files.

  • command_name (str) – Name of the “rn” script. Can be changed to custom “rn” script names.

  • capture_output (bool) – If True, capture stdout/stderr and include them in RunResult. If False, wait without collecting output (stdout/stderr in result are empty strings).

  • timeout (float | None) – Maximum time in seconds to wait before aborting. If exceeded, the process is killed and RunTimeoutError is raised.

  • observer (RunObserver | None) – RunObserver object that observes StateTransitions for status and repository admin.

  • log_file_name (str)

  • live_registry (LiveProcessRegistry | None)

Returns:

RunResult object containing information about the run after finishing.

Return type:

RunResult

mesa_runner.wait_for_model_process(model, handle, process, *, timeout=None, capture_output=True, observer=None, live_registry=None)[source]¶

Wait for a launched model process to finish and return its final run result.

This function is the completion step of the non-blocking workflow:

  1. launch_model_process() starts the run and returns immediately with (RunHandle, process).

  2. wait_for_model_process() blocks until that process exits (or times out), finalizes model state, and builds a RunResult.

Behavior:

  • Waits for process completion.

  • Optionally captures stdout/stderr.

  • Updates model state to COMPLETED, FAILED, or CANCELLED.

  • Emits observer callbacks for final state and finished result.

  • Returns a RunResult with return code, timing, output, and metadata.

Parameters:

  • model (Model) – Model associated with this run.

  • handle (RunHandle) – RunHandle returned by launch_model_process; contains run_id and launch metadata.

  • process (Popen) – Subprocess object returned by launch_model_process.

  • timeout (float | None) – Maximum time in seconds to wait before aborting. If exceeded, the process is killed and RunTimeoutError is raised.

  • capture_output (bool) – If True, capture stdout/stderr and include them in RunResult. If False, wait without collecting output (stdout/stderr in result are empty strings).

  • observer (RunObserver | None) – Optional RunObserver receiving state-transition and process-finished events.

  • live_registry (LiveProcessRegistry | None)

Returns:

RunResult describing the terminal outcome of the run.

Raises:

RunTimeoutError – If timeout is reached before process completion.

Return type:

RunResult

mesa_runner.config module¶

Configuration and environment utilities.

This module resolves MESA installation metadata and runtime shell environment.

  • MesaVersion parses and compares MESA version strings.

  • MesaConfig stores resolved MESA directory and version information.

  • setup_mesa_env configures MESA_DIR and MESASDK runtime variables for Python runs.

It also provides active-config helpers so other modules can use a shared MesaConfig context without repeatedly passing it through every call.

mesa_runner.grid_run module¶

Grid orchestration for multi-model execution.

This module provides: - run_models_local: local parallel orchestration using existing launch/wait APIs. - run_models_mpi: simple rank-split parallel execution using mpi4py. - run_models: backend dispatcher.

Design goals: - Keep behavior consistent with run.py by delegating per-model execution there. - Keep orchestration simple (FIFO queue, bounded concurrency). - Remain compatible with observer-based persistence/status adapters.

mesa_runner.options module¶

Data model and utilities for MESA defaults/inlist options.

This module defines the core in-memory representation of MESA namelist content:

  • MesaOption: one option (name, default value, current value, description, namelist)

  • DefaultsFile: all options parsed from one defaults file

  • DefaultsOptions: version-aware collection of DefaultsFile objects

  • Inlist: editable model inlist with validation, search, sync, and write support

  • UnclassifiedNamelist: unknown namelist blocks preserved during parse/write

The design separates parsing from data manipulation: parser.py creates these objects from files, while this module provides methods to inspect, set, remove, compare, synchronize, and write options.

Version-aware behavior is built in (for example kap/eos and pgbinary support), so option availability and output format follow the configured MESA version.

mesa_runner.parser module¶

Parsing utilities for MESA defaults files and inlists.

This module converts on-disk MESA text files into the in-memory option models defined in options.py:

  • parse_defaults_file() -> DefaultsFile

  • build_defaults_options() / build_defaults_options_from_config() -> DefaultsOptions

  • parse_inlist() -> Inlist

The parser is version-aware and normalizes known MESA format differences (for example kap/eos split defaults and legacy binary_pgstar vs pgbinary naming). It also supports strict/lenient handling of unknown inlist options and preserves unrecognized namelist blocks for round-trip safety.

Project-directory creation utilities for MESA runs.

mesa_runner.repository module¶

SQLite-backed persistence and live-process registry for run metadata.

This module provides:

  • RunRepository protocol: persistence API consumed by observers/status.

  • SQLiteRunRepository: concrete SQLAlchemy + SQLite implementation.

  • LiveProcessRegistry: in-memory registry for currently running subprocesses.

  • RepositoryObserver: adapter that writes run events into the repository.

Persistence and live process tracking are intentionally separated: the database stores durable history, while the live registry stores active Popen handles that cannot be persisted meaningfully.

mesa_runner.run module¶

Single-model run orchestration for foreground and background execution.

This module provides:

  • launch_model_process for non-blocking process launch.

  • wait_for_model_process for completion and result finalization.

  • run_model as the blocking convenience wrapper.

It performs preflight checks, optional model/inlist sync, lifecycle state updates, timeout handling, and observer event emission.

mesa_runner.run.launch_model_process(model, *, env=None, sync_before_run=True, default_options=None, config=None, allow_unknown_options=False, command_name='rn', log_file_name='log.out', observer=None, live_registry=None)[source]¶
Function to launch a single model in a non-blocking way.

The function performs preflight checks, starts the MESA model run and immediately returns with the RunHandle and process ID for tracking. Use this if you want to run a MESA model “in the background”.

Parameters:

  • model (Model) – Model to launch.

  • env (Mapping[str, str] | None) – Optional runtime environment to launch the MESA model into.

  • sync_before_run (bool) – If True (default), the function calls work_setup.sync_model_with_disk to update the inlist attributes of Model in case the user made any changes to the inlist files themselves. This ensures that the inlist files themselves remain the ground truth.

  • default_options (DefaultsOptions | None) – DefaultOptions object. Should be passed if sync_before_run == True.

  • config (MesaConfig | None) – MesaConfig object. Will be reconstructed on the fly if not passed.

  • allow_unknown_options (bool) – If True, give a warning about inlist options that are not found in the defaults files when syncing Model.inlists with inlists in the model directory. If False, raise an exception when inlist options are found that are not found in the defaults files.

  • command_name (str) – Name of the “rn” script. Can be changed to custom “rn” script names.

  • log_file_name (str) – Name of the terminal log file that will be placed inside the model directory. Default is “log.out”

  • observer (RunObserver | None) – RunObserver object that observes StateTransitions for status and repository admin.

  • live_registry (LiveProcessRegistry | None)

Returns:

Tuple containing RunHandle and subprocess ID.

Raises:

  • ValueError – If sync_before_run is True and no DefaultsOptions object is passed

  • RunLaunchError – If model failed to launch

Return type:

tuple[RunHandle, Popen]

mesa_runner.run.run_model(model, *, env=None, sync_before_run=True, default_options=None, config=None, allow_unknown_options=False, command_name='rn', log_file_name='log.out', capture_output=True, timeout=None, observer=None, live_registry=None)[source]¶
Function to launch a single model in a blocking way.

The function calls launch_model_process and wait_for_model_process immediately afterwards. It will only return once the model has finished running. Use this to run a MESA model “on the foreground” as you would do with a regular MESA “./rn” call in the terminal.

Parameters:

  • model (Model) – Model to run.

  • env (Mapping[str, str] | None) – Optional runtime environment to launch the MESA model into.

  • sync_before_run (bool) – If True (default), the function calls work_setup.sync_model_with_disk to update the inlist attributes of Model in case the user made any changes to the inlist files themselves. This ensures that the inlist files themselves remain the ground truth.

  • default_options (DefaultsOptions | None) – DefaultOptions object. Should be passed if sync_before_run == True.

  • config (MesaConfig | None) – MesaConfig object. Will be reconstructed on the fly if not passed.

  • allow_unknown_options (bool) – If True, give a warning about inlist options that are not found in the defaults files when syncing Model.inlists with inlists in the model directory. If False, raise an exception when inlist options are found that are not found in the defaults files.

  • command_name (str) – Name of the “rn” script. Can be changed to custom “rn” script names.

  • capture_output (bool) – If True, capture stdout/stderr and include them in RunResult. If False, wait without collecting output (stdout/stderr in result are empty strings).

  • timeout (float | None) – Maximum time in seconds to wait before aborting. If exceeded, the process is killed and RunTimeoutError is raised.

  • observer (RunObserver | None) – RunObserver object that observes StateTransitions for status and repository admin.

  • log_file_name (str)

  • live_registry (LiveProcessRegistry | None)

Returns:

RunResult object containing information about the run after finishing.

Return type:

RunResult

mesa_runner.run.wait_for_model_process(model, handle, process, *, timeout=None, capture_output=True, observer=None, live_registry=None)[source]¶

Wait for a launched model process to finish and return its final run result.

This function is the completion step of the non-blocking workflow:

  1. launch_model_process() starts the run and returns immediately with (RunHandle, process).

  2. wait_for_model_process() blocks until that process exits (or times out), finalizes model state, and builds a RunResult.

Behavior:

  • Waits for process completion.

  • Optionally captures stdout/stderr.

  • Updates model state to COMPLETED, FAILED, or CANCELLED.

  • Emits observer callbacks for final state and finished result.

  • Returns a RunResult with return code, timing, output, and metadata.

Parameters:

  • model (Model) – Model associated with this run.

  • handle (RunHandle) – RunHandle returned by launch_model_process; contains run_id and launch metadata.

  • process (Popen) – Subprocess object returned by launch_model_process.

  • timeout (float | None) – Maximum time in seconds to wait before aborting. If exceeded, the process is killed and RunTimeoutError is raised.

  • capture_output (bool) – If True, capture stdout/stderr and include them in RunResult. If False, wait without collecting output (stdout/stderr in result are empty strings).

  • observer (RunObserver | None) – Optional RunObserver receiving state-transition and process-finished events.

  • live_registry (LiveProcessRegistry | None)

Returns:

RunResult describing the terminal outcome of the run.

Raises:

RunTimeoutError – If timeout is reached before process completion.

Return type:

RunResult

mesa_runner.utils module¶

Low-level utility helpers for MESA value normalization and conversion.

This module provides conversion and comparison functions for Python and Fortran-style inlist values, including canonical formatting for output and robust semantic comparison for synchronization and equality checks.

mesa_runner.utils.normalize_inlist_value_for_output(value, sig=15)[source]¶

Normalize a value for writing to an inlist.

  • Numeric-like values are rewritten to compact Fortran d notation.

  • .true./.false. are normalized to lowercase.

  • Non-numeric strings are returned stripped.

mesa_runner.work_setup module¶

Work-directory setup, synchronization, and export utilities for models.

This module handles disk-facing model directory operations.

  • importing inlists from disk into Model objects,

  • creating model work directories with links/scripts/assets,

  • syncing in-memory Model inlists with on-disk files,

  • exporting self-contained runnable work directories.

It forms the bridge between in-memory model objects and MESA-compatible directory layouts on disk.

mesa_runner.work_setup.create_modeldir(model, projectdir_path, overwrite=False, include_additional_options=False, config=None)[source]¶
Function to create a model directory in storage for a given Model object. This model

directory contains the inlists and rn & re scripts appropriate to run it.

Parameters:

  • model (Model) – Model object to be written to the model directory

  • projectdir_path (Path | str) – path to the project directory in which this model directory will be placed. This can technically be any path, but in order to run the run the model, the mdoel directory should be placed inside a project directory containing the /src folder and Fortran executable.

  • include_additional_options (bool) – If present, include unclassified namelist blocks in all inlists written to storage (see options.Inlist and options.Unclassifiednamelist documentation)

  • config (MesaConfig | None) – MesaConfig object. Automatically detected from active config if None.

  • overwrite (bool)

Returns:

Path to model directory.

Raises:

  • FileNotFoundError if projectdir_path does not exist. –

  • OSError if rm command fails when clearing out model_dirs that need to be overwritten. –

  • ValueError if model has no inlists. –

  • FileExistsError if path directory already exists and overwite=False or if file exists at same path. –

Return type:

Path

mesa_runner.work_setup.detect_workdir_mode(model)[source]¶

Function that looks in all inlists to determine if this is a star or binary model. :param model: Model object

Returs:

WorkdirMode = “star” or “binary”

Raises:

ValueError if neither star or binary namelists are detected. –

Parameters:

model (Model)

Return type:

Literal[‘star’, ‘binary’]

mesa_runner.work_setup.export_modeldir(model_dir, export_dir, projectdir_path, *, keep_executable_symlinks=False)[source]¶
Function that creates a self-contained MESA work directory for a given model

directory and project directory. This function creates a copy of the model directroy and copies over all the files and folders from the project directory required to compile and run this model on its own. This essentially creates a portable copy of the model directory, e.g. for sharing with others.

Parameters:

  • model_dir (Path | str) – Location of the model directory

  • export_dir (Path | str) – Full target directory path for the exported workdir

  • projectdir_path (Path | str) – Location of the project directory which contains the model directory.

  • keep_executable_symlinks (bool) – if True, also copy over the Fortran executables into the exported workdir. Only recommended if you plan to run the model again locally, not recommended when moving the model elsewhere and/or sharing it.

Returns:

Path to the exported workdir.

Return type:

Path

mesa_runner.work_setup.import_inlists_from_dir(model, source_dir, default_options, config=None, *, allow_unknown_options=False)[source]¶
Function that looks for files with ‘inlist’ in their name in a given directory (non-recursively),

parses them, and adds them to model.inlists.

Parameters:

  • model (Model) – Model object which inlists attribute will be populated by the parsed inlists

  • source_dir (Path | str) – path to the directory in which the function will look for inlists

  • config (MesaConfig | None) – MesaConfig object

  • default_options (DefaultsOptions) – DefaultsOptions object

  • allow_unknown_options (bool) – If True, give a warning about inlist options that are not found in the defaults files. If False, raise an exception when inlist options are found that re not found in the defaults files.

Returns:

Model object

Raises:

FileNotFoundError is source_dir does not exist. –

Return type:

Model

mesa_runner.work_setup.sync_model_with_disk(model, default_options, config=None, *, allow_unknown_options=False)[source]¶

Ensure model.inlists matches current files in model.model_path.

Disk is treated as source of truth. If drift is detected compared to the stored model.file_snapshot, model.inlists is reloaded from disk.

Returns:

True if a reload was performed, False if model was already in sync.

Parameters:

  • model (Model)

  • default_options (DefaultsOptions)

  • config (MesaConfig | None)

  • allow_unknown_options (bool)

Return type:

bool
